obligation: TSA report of a significant security concern (cyber attack)
citation: 49 CFR 1570.203(a)(1) and (c); Appendix A to part 1570 ("Cyber Attack"); C-TRANSPORTATION-S01
trigger: Compromising, or attempting to compromise or disrupt, the company's information or technology infrastructure. Ransomware on any company system qualifies, and so does a phishing compromise of a company mailbox
deadline: As soon as possible and within 24 hours of initial discovery (company target: 12 hours)
notify: TSA Transportation Security Operations Center (TSOC) by the method TSA prescribes (telephone; number on the contact card)

obligation: TSA report of unauthorized SSI release
trigger: SSI (the 2 TSA-marked documents or company records repeating them) released to unauthorized persons, for example taken by the attacker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SSI was on an affected system or account

trigger: TSA requests location and shipping information for RSSM cars
deadline: No later than 30 minutes after the request (non-Class I)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the railroad carries no RSSM today. Becomes Yes if a customer ships PIH, explosives, or highway route-controlled radioactive material (POL-02 A.10)

obligation: FRA telephonic report of certain accidents/incidents
trigger: Only if the incident leads to an event in 225.9(a), for example a train accident with damage of $150,000 or more, or a death
deadline: Immediately (as soon as possible after the determination or estimate is made)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a reportable accident/incident results, for example during paper dispatch. A cyber attack alone is not reportable under part 225

trigger: Any reportable rail equipment, grade crossing, or injury accident/incident during the incident period
deadline: Within 30 days after the end of the month in which it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a reportable accident/incident results

trigger: A reportable hazmat incident under 171.15(b), for example a propane release that forces a public evacuation or closes a major road for an hour or more
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 12 hours after the occurrence
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a hazmat incident occurs

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee records, including certification and drug and alcohol testing records). Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (a 15-day extension is possible only for good cause provided in writing to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents (current and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if employee personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the company holds records of about 40 current and former employees

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor holding company personal information (the payroll and HR SaaS, the productivity suite, the MSP) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor determines the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (POL-02 A.5)

trigger: Affected former employees who now live outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of affected people

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and FBI
citation: No legal duty for this company today
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical (company practice: same day as the TSA report)
notify: CISA; FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and sector warning

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: Notice to the connecting Class I
trigger: Interchange is delayed, or interchange EDI may carry bad data or malicious content from a compromised company account
deadline: As soon as practical; immediately if the EDI link may be affected
notify: Class I yard office and car management office; Class I dispatcher if the interchange move is affected

obligation: TSA rail cyber directive incident report
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a covered railroad
applies_at_this_tier: No - the railroad is not in 49 CFR 1580.101 and has no TSA designation (P03 section 1.1). Recheck at each renewal

obligation: Proposed TSA surface cyber incident report
applies_at_this_tier: No - proposed rule only; no final rule as of 2026-10-05

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR part 226 (89 FR 23644); C-TRANSPORTATION-R07
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05; scope for small freight railroads depends on the final sector criteria
